messages:
nora: follow-up from the quota/fairness RFC: thinking about a small "local fairness proxy" co-located with edge proxies. idea: let the proxy perform lightweight per-tenant shaping to smooth bursts before they hit the global scheduler.

pete: can you outline the responsibilities vs the central scheduler? we don't want split-brain fairness.

nora: responsibilities: short smoothing window (100-500ms), local deficit-based token buckets, immediate reject of obvious abuse (from abuse stream), and tagging requests with local metrics for the central scheduler. central scheduler keeps the canonical fairness state and final admits.

anjali: are we describing another cache/gateway variant? what's the difference from the edge quota gateway proposals?

nora: similar but smaller scope: proxy is per-edge-process, super-low-latency, purely smoothing and telemetry tagging. no leases, no durable admits. gateway was a regional caching admission layer; local proxy is per-process smoothing to reduce microbursts.

mike: what's the smoothing algorithm? token bucket with deficit carryover? leaky bucket?

pete: proposal: deficit round-robin inspired token bucket: each tenant has budget, unused budget decays slowly into a shared pool, and proxy can borrow up to a short window. keeps fairness soft and local.

luisa: how do abuse signals factor in? we risk letting a high-abuse client exploit local smoothing.

nora: proxy subscribes to the same short-window abuse deltas and enforces immediate soft-deny if abuse_score > threshold. plus proxies report every local soft-deny to the bank for audit.

anjali: metrics and visibility? local smoothing could obscure true demand spikes. need per-request annotations.

nora: proxies attach: X-Local-Fairness-Hint (tenant_id, local_budget_delta, borrowed_flag). central scheduler ingests hints (sampled) for rebalancing. also emit per-tenant local-hit/miss, borrow-rate, and denied-by-abuse counters.

mike: failure model: if central scheduler disagrees (says tenant should be limited), we should have bank override. how fast can central react?

nora: central reacts on second timescale. proxies must honor immediate bank pushes: bank can send emergency throttle for tenant and proxies must stop smoothing within 50ms. use streaming RPC for pushes.

pete: ops: default on for hosted, opt-out for Dedicated. performance impact? tiny CPU per edge process, memory negligible. need benchmarks.

luisa: security: signed headers for hints? avoid spoofing by clients.

nora: hints are internal-only headers between edge+bank; proxies sign hints with per-node key. bank validates when ingesting. all RPCs mTLS.

anjali: rollout plan? I'd like a staged experiment: enable local smoothing in passive mode (attach hints but still forward), then active smoothing for a small % of traffic, measure unfairness regression.

mike: agree. add a chaos test where central scheduler lags and we check for divergence. also SRE runbook to flip smoothing off if error budget burns.

sre-bot: action created: INFRA-3007 "local-fairness-proxy: PoC + canary" assigned to pete,nora due 2w.

pete: next steps: implement tiny PoC in edge process (poc-mode), collect metrics for 1 week, and run sim comparing with/without smoothing.

nora: thanks all. I'll post a short design doc and link the PoC branch. :thumbsup:
